q: Did games with smaller crowds coincide with smaller national TV audiences in 2025 and 2026?
title: MLB attendance and national TV audiences, 2025-2026
report:
Yes, games with smaller crowds tended to have smaller national TV audiences, but a crowd that was small for its own park did not clearly mean a smaller audience[1]. Comparing games on the same network, the two moved together (correlation 0.34 in 2025, n = 82, range 0.14 to 0.52; 0.47 in 2026, n = 83, range 0.29 to 0.62)[1]. After comparing each game with its own park's usual crowd, the link mostly disappears (0.16 in 2025, range -0.05 to 0.37; 0.14 in 2026, range -0.08 to 0.34; both ranges include zero)[1]. Across team-seasons, teams with bigger average crowds also had bigger average national TV audiences (correlation 0.52, n = 56, range 0.30 to 0.69), which is consistent with team-level factors such as popularity and market size driving both, though the data does not prove the cause[2].

*Viewership figures are publicly reported and may differ from official Nielsen data. They are the national TV audience, excluding streaming add-ons. Nielsen changed its method on September 1, 2025, so 2025 and 2026 figures are not like-for-like.*

sources.query: SELECT headline_text FROM crowd_tv_headline

q: Why did the Mets over-perform on attendance in 2025?
title: Mets attendance above expectations, 2025
report: The New York Mets averaged 39,316 fans per game in 2025, which was 21.4% higher than what their prior two years of crowds, win rate, and market would predict, representing a 33.3% increase from the season before as a rebound from a down 2024[1]. This 2025 average attendance was higher than the 2024 average of 29,485 fans by 9,831 fans, with 94.9% of capacity in 2025 compared to 69.8% of capacity in 2024, a gap of 25.1 percentage points[1]. This surge in crowds coincided with several major events, beginning with the historic signing of outfielder Juan Soto to a 15-year, $765 million contract in December 2024[2]. On the field, the Mets held the best record in MLB at 45–24 through June 12, and on July 19, the team retired former captain David Wright's number 5 and inducted him into the Mets Hall of Fame during a pre-game ceremony at Citi Field[2].

sources.query: SELECT m2025.season AS season_2025, m2025.avg_attendance AS actual_avg_attendance_2025, m2025.expected_avg_attendance AS expected_avg_attendance_2025, m2025.residual_pct AS residual_pct_2025, m2025.yoy_change_pct AS yoy_change_pct_2025, m2025.record AS record_2025, g2025.avg_fill_pct AS avg_fill_pct_2025, m2024.season AS season_2024, m2024.avg_attendance AS actual_avg_attendance_2024, m2024.expected_avg_attendance AS expected_avg_attendance_2024, m2024.residual_pct AS residual_pct_2024, m2024.yoy_change_pct AS yoy_change_pct_2024, m2024.record AS record_2024, g2024.avg_fill_pct AS avg_fill_pct_2024, (m2025.avg_attendance - m2024.avg_attendance) AS diff_avg_attendance, (m2025.expected_avg_attendance - m2024.expected_avg_attendance) AS diff_expected_avg_attendance, (m2025.residual_pct - m2024.residual_pct) AS diff_residual_pct, (m2025.yoy_change_pct - m2024.yoy_change_pct) AS diff_yoy_change_pct, (g2025.avg_fill_pct - g2024.avg_fill_pct) AS diff_avg_fill_pct FROM team_season_model m2025 JOIN team_season_model m2024 ON m2025.team_id = m2024.team_id AND m2024.season = 2024 JOIN (SELECT season, avg(fill_pct) as avg_fill_pct FROM games_clean WHERE home_team = 'New York Mets' GROUP BY season) g2025 ON g2025.season = 2025 JOIN (SELECT season, avg(fill_pct) as avg_fill_pct FROM games_clean WHERE home_team = 'New York Mets' GROUP BY season) g2024 ON g2024.season = 2024 WHERE m2025.team_id = 121 AND m2025.season = 2025

q: What drives MLB attendance?

chart.title: Game factors associated with attendance
labels: Games with a closed roof or dome
chart.note: Each bar is compared with its own baseline: Friday for days, August for months, and the average opponent for opponents. Only the largest clear associations are shown.

title: What drives MLB attendance, 2024 to 2026
report: A 69.1% turnout bump coincided with home openers compared to regular games, while hosting the Los Angeles Dodgers was associated with a 25.0% larger crowd compared to the average opponent[1]. Matchups against the New York Yankees and Chicago Cubs also coincided with turnout bumps of 15.7% and 13.1% respectively, compared to the average opponent[1]. Saturdays were associated with an 8.8% larger crowd compared to Fridays, while Mondays, Wednesdays, Tuesdays, and Thursdays coincided with turnout drops of 21.8%, 20.6%, 18.9%, and 16.6% respectively[1]. Sunday games showed an unclear drop of 1.0%[1]. For months, July and June dates coincided with turnout bumps of 4.2% and 2.5% compared to August, while March and April games were associated with a 10.9% drop, May games with a 3.1% drop, and September games with an unclear 0.3% drop[1]. On a season level, a record about 16 wins better in a 162-game season was associated with an 8.8% larger yearly turnout, while a 10% higher crowd over the prior two years coincided with an 8.0% larger crowd[2]. A 10% larger metro population was associated with an unclear 0.2% bump, and stadium age was not included in the model[1]. Overall, team-level factors accounted for 90.5% of the differences in season attendance (n = 86), while game-level factors accounted for 82.6% of the variation across individual dates, or 43.2% when looking within the same venue and season, with a prediction error of 0.2 compared to a baseline of 0.3 (n = 7,205)[3].

q: How did Cubs attendance change by month in 2025?
title: Cubs attendance by month, 2025
report: The Chicago Cubs saw their home crowds peak in June during the 2025 season, with average attendance rising through the spring before steadily declining into September[1]. In April, the team drew a total of 474,334 fans, with an average of 33,881 fans per game, which represented 82.0% of capacity[1]. May total attendance rose by 38,851 fans to 513,185, representing an average of 36,656 fans (an increase of 2,775 in average attendance) and 88.8% of capacity, a jump of 6.7 percentage points[2]. June reached the season's highest average of 39,531 fans per game (95.7% of capacity), growing by 2,875 in average attendance and 7.0 percentage points, though total attendance fell by 117,875 fans to 395,310[2]. July's average attendance dipped by 247 fans to an average of 39,284 fans (95.1% of capacity, a 0.6 percentage point drop), but total attendance grew by 76,103 fans to 471,413[2]. August's average attendance dropped by 1,069 fans to an average of 38,216 fans (92.6% of capacity, a 2.6 percentage point decrease) while total attendance rose by 63,609 fans to 535,022[2]. September finished with a total of 543,987 fans, an increase of 8,965, but the average fell by 1,950 fans to an average of 36,266 fans per game, representing 87.8% of capacity after a 4.7 percentage point drop[2].

sources.query: SELECT EXTRACT(MONTH FROM official_date) AS month, COUNT(*) AS games_count, AVG(attendance) AS avg_attendance, SUM(attendance) AS total_attendance, AVG(fill_pct) AS avg_fill_pct FROM games_clean WHERE home_team_id = 112 AND season = 2025 GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

q: How did average attendance differ by weekday across MLB in 2025?
title: MLB average attendance by weekday, 2025
report: An average of 33,568 fans attended Saturday MLB games in 2025, representing the weekly peak at 82.9% of capacity[1]. Friday was the next highest, averaging 32,198 fans at 79.7% of capacity, which was 1,371 fewer fans than Saturday and a gap of 3.2 percentage points[1]. Sunday games averaged 30,948 fans at 76.8% of capacity, trailing Saturday by 2,620 fans with a gap of 6.1 percentage points[1]. Thursday games averaged 28,151 fans at 70.2% of capacity, which was 5,417 fewer fans than Saturday and a gap of 12.8 percentage points[1]. Tuesday games averaged 26,644 fans at 67.1% of capacity, trailing Saturday by 6,924 fans with a gap of 15.8 percentage points[1]. Monday games averaged 26,397 fans at 66.4% of capacity, which was 7,172 fewer fans than Saturday and a gap of 16.5 percentage points[1]. Wednesday games were the lowest of the week, averaging 26,140 fans at 65.7% of capacity, trailing Saturday by 7,429 fans with a gap of 17.2 percentage points[1].

sources.query: WITH weekday_stats AS ( SELECT weekday, AVG(attendance) AS avg_attendance, AVG(fill_pct) AS avg_fill_pct FROM games_clean WHERE season = 2025 GROUP BY weekday ), saturday AS ( SELECT avg_attendance AS sat_att, avg_fill_pct AS sat_fill FROM weekday_stats WHERE weekday = 'Saturday' ), wednesday AS ( SELECT avg_attendance AS wed_att, avg_fill_pct AS wed_fill FROM weekday_stats WHERE weekday = 'Wednesday' ) SELECT w.weekday, w.avg_attendance, w.avg_fill_pct, w.avg_attendance - s.sat_att AS attendance_diff_vs_saturday, w.avg_fill_pct - s.sat_fill AS fill_diff_vs_saturday FROM weekday_stats w, saturday s ORDER BY w.avg_attendance DESC

data_note: Data sources: MLB Stats API (statsapi.mlb.com).

q: Compare actual and expected average attendance for the five AL East teams in 2025.

chart.title: Actual and expected attendance by name

title: AL East actual vs expected attendance, 2025
report: Boston was the only AL East team to exceed its expected average attendance in 2025, drawing 34,278 fans per game, which was 511 fans (1.5%) above expectations and filled 90.8% of capacity[1]. The New York Yankees led the division with 42,408 fans per game, but this was 827 fans (1.9%) below their expected average of 43,235, filling 91.1% of capacity[1]. The Toronto Blue Jays averaged 35,184 fans per game, falling 1,639 fans (4.5%) short of their expected average of 36,823, while filling 89.9% of capacity[1]. The Baltimore Orioles averaged 22,546 fans per game, which was 3,174 fans (12.3%) below their expected average of 25,720, filling 49.9% of capacity[1]. The Tampa Bay Rays averaged 9,713 fans per game and filled 88.1% of capacity, but their expected average is unknown because they played at Steinbrenner Field, a temporary park[1].

sources.query: SELECT t.name, ts.avg_attendance, ts.expected_avg_attendance, (ts.avg_attendance - ts.expected_avg_attendance) AS difference, ts.residual_pct, AVG(g.fill_pct) AS avg_fill_pct FROM team_season_model ts JOIN teams t ON ts.team_id = t.team_id AND ts.season = t.season LEFT JOIN games_clean g ON g.home_team_id = ts.team_id AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM g.official_date) = ts.season WHERE ts.season = 2025 AND t.division = 'American League East' GROUP BY t.name, ts.avg_attendance, ts.expected_avg_attendance, ts.residual_pct ORDER BY t.name;

data_note: Data sources: MLB Stats API (statsapi.mlb.com).

q: Rank the networks by average national TV audience in 2026.
title: MLB national TV audience by network, 2026
report:
Fox led all national TV networks in average viewership for the season, followed in order by Netflix, NBC, ABC, ESPN, TBS, and FS1[1]. Fox averaged 2,343,875 viewers across 24 windows with known audiences in 2026[1]. Netflix averaged 2,314,000 viewers across 2 games with known audiences in 2026[1]. NBC averaged 2,312,762 viewers across 21 games with known audiences in 2026[1]. ABC averaged 1,794,333 viewers across 3 games with known audiences in 2026[1]. ESPN averaged 1,126,208 viewers across 24 games with known audiences in 2026, out of 27 games[1]. TBS averaged 614,900 viewers across 10 games with known audiences in 2026, out of 25 games[1]. FS1 averaged 385,905 viewers across 21 games with known audiences in 2026, out of 39 games[1].

*Viewership figures are publicly reported and may differ from official Nielsen data. They are the national TV audience, excluding streaming add-ons.*

q: How did Yankees attendance change from 2024 to 2025?
title: Yankees attendance, 2024 vs 2025
report: The New York Yankees drew 3,392,659 home fans in 2025, which was 82,821 more than their 2024 total of 3,309,838[1]. Their average home attendance rose by 511 fans to 42,408 per game in 2025, up from 41,897 in 2024[1]. This growth coincided with a higher average fill rate of 91.1% in 2025 compared to 90.1% of capacity in 2024[2].

sources.query: SELECT season, official_home_total, avg_attendance, model_games FROM team_season_model WHERE team_id = 147 AND season IN (2024, 2025) ORDER BY season

q: Compare Dodgers attendance in 2024, 2025 and 2026.

chart.title: Average attendance by month, 2024 vs 2025 vs 2026

title: Dodgers attendance, 2024 to 2026
report: The Los Angeles Dodgers consistently grew their home crowds from 2024 to 2026, culminating in a peak average of 49,805 fans per game in 2026[1]. In 2024, the Dodgers averaged 48,657 fans, which was 3.7% below what their record and market predicted, a 2.7% increase from the prior season[1]. In 2025, they averaged 49,537 fans, which was 3.0% above what was predicted, a 1.8% increase from the prior season[1]. In 2026, they averaged 49,805 fans, which was 1.2% below what was predicted, a 0.5% increase from the prior season[1]. This growth coincided with the average fill rate rising by 0.8 percentage points from 2024 (87.6% of capacity) to 2025 (88.5% of capacity), and by another 0.5 percentage points in 2026 (88.9% of capacity)[2]. Total attendance in clean games grew by 87,147 fans from 2024 to 2025, and by 21,749 fans from 2025 to 2026[2]. The team went 98-64 in 2024, 93-69 in 2025, and 100-62 in 2026[1]. Outside of regular home games, the 2024 Seoul Series special event drew 15,928 fans, or 95.1% of capacity[3].

sources.query: SELECT season, avg_attendance, expected_avg_attendance, residual_pct, record, yoy_change_pct, official_home_total, avg_attendance - LAG(avg_attendance) OVER (ORDER BY season) AS yoy_diff_attendance FROM team_season_model WHERE team_id = 119 AND season BETWEEN 2024 AND 2026 ORDER BY season;

SELECT season, avg(fill_pct) AS avg_fill_pct, sum(attendance) AS total_attendance, sum(capacity_used) AS total_capacity, LAG(avg(fill_pct)) OVER (ORDER BY season) AS prev_avg_fill_pct, avg(fill_pct) - LAG(avg(fill_pct)) OVER (ORDER BY season) AS yoy_diff_avg_fill_pct, LAG(sum(attendance)) OVER (ORDER BY season) AS prev_total_attendance, sum(attendance) - LAG(sum(attendance)) OVER (ORDER BY season) AS yoy_diff_total_attendance, LAG(sum(capacity_used)) OVER (ORDER BY season) AS prev_total_capacity, sum(capacity_used) - LAG(sum(capacity_used)) OVER (ORDER BY season) AS yoy_diff_total_capacity FROM games_clean WHERE home_team = 'Los Angeles Dodgers' GROUP BY season ORDER BY season;
SELECT * FROM games WHERE (home_team_id = 119 OR away_team_id = 119) AND official_date = '2024-03-21'

q: List the five biggest Cubs home crowds in 2025, with date, opponent and attendance.
title: Cubs five biggest home crowds, 2025
report: The Chicago Cubs drew their five largest home crowds of 2025 against the Brewers, Red Sox, Mariners, and Orioles, peaking at 41,078 fans on June 19[1]. That top game against the Milwaukee Brewers represented 99.5% of the park's 41,298 capacity, followed by 41,011 fans against the Boston Red Sox on July 18 at 99.3% of capacity, 40,787 fans against the Seattle Mariners on June 20 at 98.8% of capacity, 40,781 fans against the Baltimore Orioles on August 2 at 98.7% of capacity, and 40,703 fans against the Red Sox on July 19 at 98.6% of capacity[1].

sources.query: SELECT official_date, away_team, attendance, capacity_used, fill_pct FROM games_clean WHERE home_team_id = 112 AND season = 2025 ORDER BY attendance DESC LIMIT 5

q: Do popular teams explain the link between crowds and TV audiences?
title: Popular teams, attendance and TV audiences, 2024 to 2026
report:
Yes, games with smaller crowds tended to have smaller national TV audiences, but a crowd that was small for its own park did not clearly mean a smaller audience[1]. Comparing games on the same network, the two moved together (correlation 0.34 in 2025, n = 82, range 0.14 to 0.52; 0.47 in 2026, n = 83, range 0.29 to 0.62)[1]. After comparing each game with its own park's usual crowd, the link mostly disappears (0.16 in 2025, range -0.05 to 0.37; 0.14 in 2026, range -0.08 to 0.34; both ranges include zero)[1]. Across team-seasons, teams with bigger average crowds also had bigger average national TV audiences (correlation 0.52, n = 56, range 0.30 to 0.69), which is consistent with team-level factors such as popularity and market size driving both, though the data does not prove the cause[2].

*Viewership figures are publicly reported and may differ from official Nielsen data. They are the national TV audience, excluding streaming add-ons. Nielsen changed its method on September 1, 2025, so 2025 and 2026 figures are not like-for-like.*

q: How much does a team's winning go with higher attendance?
title: What drives MLB attendance
report: An 8.8% higher team-level attendance was associated with a season record about 16 wins better in a 162-game season (p-value = 0.0; table: model_coefficients), according to a team-level model of fan turnout ($n = 86$, $R^2 = 0.91$; table: model_fit)[1]. A 4.7% higher crowd at the game level coincided with a win rate worth about 16 more wins in a 162-game season (p-value = 0.0; table: model_coefficients), in a model tracking game-by-game attendance ($n = 7,205$, $R^2 = 0.83$, with a within-venue-season $R^2 = 0.43$ and a cross-validated RMSE log of 0.2; table: model_fit)[2].

sources.query: SELECT * FROM model_coefficients WHERE model = 'game'
rows: Night games, compared with day games

sources.query: SELECT * FROM model_fit

q: How did Yankees national TV audiences change from 2025 to 2026?
title: Yankees national TV audience, 2025 vs 2026
report:
The New York Yankees grew their average national TV audience by 533,238 viewers from 2025 to 2026, climbing to an average of 1,694,167 viewers per single game, though Nielsen changed its method in September 2025, which generally raised sports audiences[1]. During the 2025 season, the team made 19 national TV appearances with 14 single games, averaging 1,160,929 viewers and peaking at 2,784,000 viewers[1]. Their 2025 games were broadcast across a network mix of seven games on TBS, five each on ESPN and Fox, and two on FS1[1]. In 2026, the Yankees increased their national presence to 22 appearances and 17 single games, while their highest-viewed single game reached 3,616,000 viewers[1]. The team's 2026 network mix also diversified, featuring eight games on TBS, five on Fox, three on NBC, two each on ESPN and FS1, and one each on ABC and Netflix[1].

*Viewership figures are publicly reported and may differ from official Nielsen data. They are the national TV audience, excluding streaming add-ons.*

sources.query: SELECT season, appearances, single_games, avg_single_game_viewers, highest_single_game_viewers, network_mix, (SELECT avg_single_game_viewers FROM team_tv_summary t2 WHERE t2.team_id = 147 AND t2.season = 2026) - (SELECT avg_single_game_viewers FROM team_tv_summary t1 WHERE t1.team_id = 147 AND t1.season = 2025) as diff_avg_viewers FROM team_tv_summary WHERE team_id = 147 ORDER BY season
rows: TBS 8, Fox 5, NBC 3, ESPN 2, FS1 2, ABC 1, Netflix 1

q: Compare the Cubs and White Sox on attendance and national TV audiences in 2025.
title: Cubs and White Sox attendance and TV audience, 2025
report:
The Chicago Cubs dominated the Chicago White Sox in both local turnout and national television exposure during the 2025 season, drawing 19,187 more fans per game and securing 17 national TV appearances while the White Sox had none[1].

### Attendance
The Chicago Cubs drew an average of 37,259 fans per game in 2025, which was 19,187 more than the Chicago White Sox average of 18,072 fans[1]. This turnout put the Cubs at 89.9% of capacity, while the White Sox filled just 45.0% of capacity, representing a gap of 44.9 percentage points[1].

### National TV Audiences
For their 12 single-game broadcasts, the Cubs averaged 1,030,818 viewers, peaking at 2,041,000 viewers for their highest-rated game[2]. The Cubs' national lineup featured six games on Fox, five on ESPN, three on FS1, and three on TBS[3].

*Viewership figures are publicly reported and may differ from official Nielsen data. They are the national TV audience, excluding streaming add-ons.*

sources.query: WITH metrics AS ( SELECT home_team_id, home_team, avg(attendance) as g_avg_attendance, avg(fill_pct) as g_avg_fill_pct FROM games_clean WHERE season = 2025 AND home_team_id IN (112, 145) GROUP BY home_team_id, home_team ) SELECT cubs.home_team AS team_cubs, cubs.g_avg_attendance AS cubs_game_avg_attendance, cubs.g_avg_fill_pct AS cubs_game_avg_fill_pct, ts_cubs.avg_attendance AS cubs_model_avg_attendance, ts_cubs.expected_avg_attendance AS cubs_expected_avg_attendance, sox.home_team AS team_sox, sox.g_avg_attendance AS sox_game_avg_attendance, sox.g_avg_fill_pct AS sox_game_avg_fill_pct, ts_sox.avg_attendance AS sox_model_avg_attendance, ts_sox.expected_avg_attendance AS sox_expected_avg_attendance, -- Differences (Cubs minus White Sox) cubs.g_avg_attendance - sox.g_avg_attendance AS diff_game_avg_attendance, cubs.g_avg_fill_pct - sox.g_avg_fill_pct AS diff_game_avg_fill_pct, ts_cubs.avg_attendance - ts_sox.avg_attendance AS diff_model_avg_attendance, ts_cubs.expected_avg_attendance - ts_sox.expected_avg_attendance AS diff_expected_avg_attendance FROM metrics cubs JOIN team_season_model ts_cubs ON ts_cubs.team_id = 112 AND ts_cubs.season = 2025 CROSS JOIN metrics sox JOIN team_season_model ts_sox ON ts_sox.team_id = 145 AND ts_sox.season = 2025 WHERE cubs.home_team_id = 112 AND sox.home_team_id = 145
